ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A Germanium sample of dimensions \(1cm \times 1cm\) is illuminated with a 20 mW, 600 nm laser light source as shown in the figure. The illuminated sample surface has a 100 nm of lossless Silicon dioxide layer that reflects one-fourth of the incident light. From the remaining light, one-third of the power is reflected from the Silicon dioxide-Germanium interface, one-third is absorbed in the Germanium layer, and one-third is transmitted through the other side of the sample. If the absorption coefficient of Germanium at 600 nm is \(3 \times 10^4 cm^{-1}\) and the bandgap is 0.66 eV, the thickness of the Germanium layer, rounded off to 3 decimal places, is ______ \(\mu m\).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The two attached figures show the same structural schematic: a sample block whose upper surface is about 1 cm × 1 cm, with a downward incident laser arrow on the top, labeled 20 mW, 600 nm. The upper layer of the sample is labeled Silicon dioxide, and the thickness of this layer is marked on the right as 100 nm; below it is the Germanium layer, and the thickness T to be found is marked on the right. Reasoning: According to the power distribution given in the problem, let the incident power P0 = 20 mW. The top surface of SiO2 first reflects P0/4, and the remaining 3P0/4 reaches the SiO2-Ge interface. The problem states that among this remaining light, 1/3 is reflected by the interface, 1/3 is absorbed in Ge, and 1/3 is transmitted from the other side of the sample, so the absorbed power in Ge is equal to the final transmitted power. The power truly entering Ge is the absorbed power plus the transmitted power, denoted as Pin. When passing through Ge of thickness T, the absorbed power is Pin[1 - exp(-αT)], and the transmitted power is Pin exp(-αT). Because the two are equal, Pin[1 - exp(-αT)] = Pin exp(-αT). Canceling Pin gives 1 - exp(-αT) = exp(-αT), that is exp(-αT) = 1/2, therefore T = ln(2)/α. Substituting α = 3 × 10^4 cm^-1, T = 0.693147/(3 × 10^4) cm = 2.31049 × 10^-5 cm. Convert to micrometers: 1 cm = 10^4 μm, so T = 0.231049 μm, rounded to 3 decimal places as 0.231 μm.

method.method_draft: Describe the figure, then use the text fractions. Start with P0=20 mW. The SiO2 top surface reflects P0/4, leaving 3P0/4 at the SiO2-Ge interface. Of this remaining light, one-third is reflected at the interface, one-third is absorbed in Ge, and one-third is transmitted, so the absorbed power and final transmitted power are equal. The power that actually enters the Ge is the sum of absorbed plus transmitted powers. Therefore set P_in[1-exp(-alpha T)] = P_in exp(-alpha T). Cancel P_in, solve exp(-alpha T)=1/2, so T=ln(2)/alpha with alpha=3e4 cm^-1. Convert the result from cm to micrometers and round to 3 decimals.

method.method_draft: Describe the figure, then reason in terms of photon probabilities rather than mW. method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中显示一束标注为 20 mW、600 nm 的光从上方向下照射到样品顶部。样品顶部平面标注为 1 cm × 1 cm。右侧剖面显示上层是 Silicon dioxide，厚度标注为 100 nm；下层是 Germanium，厚度标注为 T。

推理：按题意，SiO2 顶表面先反射掉入射光的 1/4，剩余光到达 SiO2-Ge 界面。在这部分剩余光中，1/3 在 SiO2-Ge 界面反射，1/3 被 Ge 吸收，1/3 从样品另一侧透射。去掉界面反射的部分后，进入 Ge 的光子中，被吸收的光子数与最终透射的光子数相等。

600 nm 光子的能量约为 1240/600 = 2.067 eV，大于 Ge 的带隙 0.66 eV，因此可用给定吸收系数描述吸收。设 Ge 厚度为 T，透射概率为 exp(-alpha T)，吸收概率为 1 - exp(-alpha T)。由于吸收概率等于透射概率：
1 - exp(-alpha T) = exp(-alpha T)。
所以 2 exp(-alpha T) = 1，得到 alpha T = ln 2。

alpha = 3 × 10^4 cm^-1，因此 T = ln 2 / (3 × 10^4) cm = 2.31049 × 10^-5 cm。换算为微米：1 cm = 10^4 micrometers，所以 T = 0.231049 micrometers。四舍五入到 3 位小数为 0.231 micrometers。

If the absorption coefficient of Germanium at 600 nm is \(3 \times 10^4\, cm^{-1}\) and the bandgap is 0.66 eV, the thickness of the Germanium layer, rounded off to 3 decimal places, is ______ \(\mu m\).
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A Germanium sample of dimensions \(1\, cm \times 1\, cm\) is illuminated with a 20 mW, 600 nm laser light source as shown in the figure. The illuminated sample surface has a 100 nm lossless Silicon dioxide layer that reflects one-fourth of the incident light. From the remaining light, one-third of the power is reflected from the Silicon dioxide-Germanium interface, one-third is absorbed in the Germanium layer, and one-third is transmitted through the other side of the sample. If the absorption coefficient of Germanium at 600 nm is \(3 \times 10^4\, cm^{-1}\) and the bandgap is 0.66 eV, the thickness of the Germanium layer, rounded off to 3 decimal places, is ______ \(\mu m\).
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The two attached figures show the same structural schematic: a sample block whose upper surface is about 1 cm × 1 cm, with a downward incident laser arrow on the top, labeled 20 mW, 600 nm. The upper layer of the sample is labeled Silicon dioxide, and the thickness of this layer is marked on the right as 100 nm; below it is the Germanium layer, and the thickness T to be found is marked on the right. Reasoning: According to the power distribution given in the problem, let the incident power P0 = 20 mW. The top surface of SiO2 first reflects P0/4, and the remaining 3P0/4 reaches the SiO2-Ge interface. The problem states that among this remaining light, 1/3 is reflected by the interface, 1/3 is absorbed in Ge, and 1/3 is transmitted from the other side of the sample, so the absorbed power in Ge is equal to the final transmitted power. The power truly entering Ge is the absorbed power plus the transmitted power, denoted as Pin. When passing through Ge of thickness T, the absorbed power is Pin[1 - exp(-αT)], and the transmitted power is Pin exp(-αT). Because the two are equal, Pin[1 - exp(-αT)] = Pin exp(-αT). Canceling Pin gives 1 - exp(-αT) = exp(-αT), that is exp(-αT) = 1/2, therefore T = ln(2)/α. Substituting α = 3 × 10^4 cm^-1, T = 0.693147/(3 × 10^4) cm = 2.31049 × 10^-5 cm. Convert to micrometers: 1 cm = 10^4 μm, so T = 0.231049 μm, rounded to 3 decimal places as 0.231 μm.
